operative_text.controlling:
10.45(1)  After hearing an appeal from an assessment officer’s
decision, the judge may, by order, do one or more of the following:
(a) confirm, vary or revoke the decision;
(b) revoke the decision and substitute a decision;
(c) revoke all or part of the decision and refer the matter back
to the same or another assessment officer;
(d) make any other order the judge considers appropriate.
(2)  If the amount of costs payable as originally assessed by the
assessment officer has been paid and, after payment, is reduced on
appeal, the judge hearing the appeal may order the return of the
excess by the party who has received it and the order may be
enforced as an order of the Court.

BOOK_A.title: Decision of the Judge
BOOK_A.operative_text_raw:
10.45(1) After hearing an appeal from an assessment ofﬁcer’s decision, the
judge may, by order, do one or more of the following:
(a) conﬁrm, vary or revoke the decision;
(b) revoke the decision and substitute a decision;
(c) revoke all or part of the decision and refer the matter back to the
same or another assessment ofﬁcer;
(d) make any other order the judge considers appropriate.
(2) If the amount of costs payable as originally assessed by the assessment
ofﬁcer has been paid and, after payment, is reduced on appeal, the judge hearing
the appeal may order the return of the excess by the party who has received it
and the order may be enforced as an order of the Court.⁵
[Alta. Reg.124/10;163/10]
BOOK_A.commentary:
An appeal from an Assessment Ofﬁcer is on the record and gets deference because of the
Assessment Ofﬁcer’s experience and knowledge.⁶

footnotes.text: Quite similar to previous 1968 R.648(3). It came from 1944 C. R.780, as amended by Alta. Reg.86/60. New R.10.45(2) was enacted by Alta. Reg.163/2010.
